_note: Plates that are not plain public domain. Public domain is the default and is not listed here; this file records the ones that carry an obligation, so the colophon credit can be checked instead of remembered. `credit` must appear in templates/shell.html verbatim — `npm run check` fails if it does not, because the licence requires it and a missing credit is a breach, not an untidiness. Values for `licence`: a CC identifier, or `loc-no-known-restrictions` for the narrower claim the Library of Congress actually makes. Re-check when a plate is replaced.

mandela.credit: the Mandela photograph is by South Africa The Good News (sagoodnews.co.za) under CC BY 2.0

steve-jobs.credit: the Steve Jobs photograph was taken at WWDC in 2010 by Matthew Yohe under CC BY-SA 3.0

tu-youyou.credit: the Tu Youyou photograph was taken in Stockholm on 6 December 2015 by Bengt Nyman under CC BY-SA 4.0

robert-moses.by: C. M. Stieglitz, New York World-Telegram & Sun
robert-moses.credit: the 1939 photograph of Robert Moses is by C. M. Stieglitz for the New York World-Telegram & Sun, held by the Library of Congress, which states that it knows of no copyright restrictions on it

rosalind-franklin.by: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, from the personal collection of Jenifer Glynn
rosalind-franklin.credit: the 1955 photograph of Rosalind Franklin at her microscope is credited to the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, from the personal collection of her sister Jenifer Glynn, under CC BY-SA 4.0

wu-chien-shiung.credit: the 1963 photograph of Wu Chien-Shiung at Columbia comes from the Smithsonian Institution Archives, published with no known copyright restrictions

frances-kelsey.credit: the photograph of Frances Kelsey receiving her award from President Kennedy comes from the National Library of Medicine, which believes the item to be in the public domain

frances-perkins.credit: the April 1936 photograph of Frances Perkins is by Harris & Ewing, held by the Library of Congress, which states that it knows of no copyright restrictions on it

samuel-zemurray.credit: the photograph of Samuel Zemurray, taken on 10 January 1934 for the Los Angeles Times, is from the Los Angeles Times Photographic Collection at UCLA Library Special Collections, under CC BY 4.0

edwin-land.credit: the photograph of Edwin Land presenting at Polaroid is by Bernard Gotfryd, held by the Library of Congress, which states that there are no known restrictions on its publication

thomas-midgley-jr.credit: the 1930s studio portrait of Thomas Midgley Jr. by Blank & Stoller of New York comes from the Science History Institute, which reasonably believes it is not restricted by copyright but says a conclusive determination could not be made

annie-turnbo-malone.credit: the photograph of Annie Turnbo Malone is from a Poro College souvenir booklet printed between 1920 and 1927, held by the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African American History and Culture, which lists no known copyright restrictions on it

henry-ford.credit: the photograph of Henry Ford, about 1919, is by Fred Hartsook, from the National Photo Company collection at the Library of Congress, which states that there are no known copyright restrictions on its use
